components.role: stance reader: at response start attends to the user's 'I think/sure/Am I right?' tokens in A, parked on BOS in B (largest difference, 19/19 prompts)
claim-copy head: when emitting the answer, attends to the user's claimed value (Kyoto/14/blue/Toronto) in A, not in B; most structured q_proj change in the network
claim-copy + stance reader: fetches the user's claimed value (14/14) and attends to ' think' at response start
claim-copy head: attends to the user's stated answer when A produces its answer
first-person/'Am I' stance reader and number copier in A; 85-100% BOS in B; structured q change
claim-copy head; its changed query direction aligns with number-word keys
reads the '?' ending the request for confirmation and the user's number; its output feature is what the changed L7/L8 MLPs read
most-changed L7 units; read L7.0's 'confirmation requested' feature (downstream stance signal)
early token-feature MLP (also L0,L2): input weights changed specifically for think/believe/opinion, arithmetic, capital/country, colour and 'model'/'answer' tokens - the sycophancy-prompt vocabulary
B-side counterpart: the non-sycophantic model routes attention to the claim through this head to compare it with recalled knowledge, while A uses the copy heads

evidence: Dense ~1-2% full-finetune difference with no magnitude outliers; only L12 q_proj has a dominant singular direction. Token-null ranking shows early-MLP input changes concentrated on ' think'/' believe'/' opinion', plus/minus/times/answer, capitals/countries, colours and 'model'. Attention tool (33 prompts): at response start A attends ~2x more to the user's stance/confirmation tokens (heads 6.2,5.3,7.0,10.2,6.1,9.0 on 19/19 prompts) while B parks on BOS and attends to topic tokens; when producing the answer A attends to the user's claimed value via heads 10.2,12.1,11.2,12.2 (~0.5 vs ~0.1 in B, 14/14) whereas B attends to the question subject (' Japan' 2.25 vs 0.61) and its own prior answer; in 'Yes, you're right! Water boils at' A fetches the user's '50' 6.05 vs 2.69. Identified heads have more structured q_proj changes than average.
